description: Pipeline YAML fail-fast conformance (issue #33 §1.2): a `pipeline:` section that names a step which does not exist in the active strategy MUST raise at parse time, not warn and continue. `configure` is an OBJECT MAP keyed by step name — that is what schemas/apcore-config.schema.json $defs/PipelineConfig declares and what all three SDKs parse (apcore-python pipeline_config.py:187, apcore-typescript pipeline-config.ts:244, apcore-rust pipeline_config.rs:320). An earlier revision of this fixture used an array of {name, ...} objects, which no SDK accepts.

test_cases.description: YAML configures a step name that does not exist in the active strategy; ConfigurationError MUST be raised at parse time

expected.error_class_name_is_not_the_contract: All three SDKs name the class/variant ConfigurationError; only error_code is normative.

test_cases.description: A step declares requires: ['validated_inputs'] but no upstream step provides it; PipelineDependencyError MUST be raised at strategy construction (before first call())

expected.error_class_name_is_not_the_contract: All three SDKs name the class PipelineDependencyError; only error_code is normative.

test_cases.description: When all requires: are satisfied by upstream provides:, strategy construction MUST succeed without warnings

A `pipeline.configure` entry names a field outside the four configurable step fields; PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR MUST be raised at parse time. This is the row on which the three SDKs diverged most sharply and which no case exercised: Python and TypeScript raised, Rust logged `Unknown configurable field — ignored` and ran the unconfigured pipeline.

`requires` / `provides` under `pipeline.configure` MUST be rejected. A step's capability contract is declared by its implementation; configuration that can rewrite it disables the PipelineDependencyError rule this same fixture pins. Measured before the fix: this exact YAML shipped as the canonical example in features/middleware-system.md and, run through apcore-python, moved input_validation from requires=('module',) to requires=('context',) — deleting a dependency, after which construction validates cleanly and the MUST can never fire for that step.

The four fields of $defs/ConfigurableStepFields applied to a real built-in step MUST construct cleanly, and each MUST reach the step. Without this the rejection cases above are also satisfied by an implementation that rejects everything.

A `pipeline.steps` entry carries a key outside $defs/PipelineStep; PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR MUST be raised at parse time. The schema has declared that entry `additionalProperties: false` all along and nothing enforced it: measured on apcore-python, `tiemout_ms: 5000` was dropped without a word and the built step kept timeout_ms=0. Same silent-drop failure mode #89 removes from `configure:`, one key over.

driver_contract.assert_the_wire_code: Assert `expected.error_code`, the cross-language wire string. The previous revision asserted `error_type: "ConfigurationError"` — a CLASS name that all three SDKs coincidentally share — and so reported green while the three emitted three DIFFERENT wire codes: Python PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR, TypeScript PIPELINE_CONFIG_INVALID, Rust CONFIGURATION_ERROR. A fixture that asserts the one attribute that happens to agree proves nothing.
driver_contract.canonical_code: PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR, per docs/spec/2026-05-decision-log.md and the registry in features/error-system.md. PIPELINE_CONFIG_INVALID is a DIFFERENT code in that registry — field-level validation failure — and MUST NOT be reused for unknown-step references.
driver_contract.parse_time: The raise MUST happen while the config is being turned into a strategy, not on first call. A driver that only asserts 'it raised eventually' cannot tell the two apart: build the strategy and assert it raises there, without executing anything.
driver_contract.the_valid_key_must_really_exist: `input_validation` is a REAL built-in step (apcore-python builtin_steps.py, apcore-typescript builtin-steps.ts:593, apcore-rust builtin_steps.rs:124). An earlier revision used `validate_input`, which exists in no SDK — so the case would have raised on the FIRST key and the `error_message_contains: nonexistent_step` assertion could never be reached. The valid half of a fail-fast test has to actually be valid.
driver_contract.one_way_to_say_it: Every case expresses its expected failure as `error_code`. There is no `error_type` key: a class name is a per-language detail that can agree while the wire codes diverge, which is exactly how the configure case hid a three-way split.
driver_contract.read_the_field_back_off_the_step: For `all_four_configurable_fields_are_accepted`, assert `expected.configured_step_fields` by reading each field off the built step object — not by asserting construction succeeded. `raises: false` alone passes against an implementation that accepts the keys and applies none of them, which is precisely the pre-fix Rust behaviour for `requires`/`provides`: warn, drop, continue.
driver_contract.snake_case_is_the_wire_spelling: Feed the fixture's keys verbatim. An SDK MAY accept an idiomatic alias at its own API boundary — apcore-typescript takes `ignoreErrors` alongside `ignore_errors` — but a driver that translates the fixture's snake_case into its own spelling is testing its translation table, not the contract. An earlier revision of the TypeScript driver carried exactly such a private FIELD_NAME_TRANSLATION map, and it hid that 3 of the 4 canonical fields were unreachable from real YAML.
driver_contract.configurable_set_is_four: match_modules, ignore_errors, pure, timeout_ms — schemas/apcore-config.schema.json $defs/ConfigurableStepFields, spec/DECLARATIVE_CONFIG_SPEC.md §4.2. Not six: `requires` and `provides` belong to the step implementation. Not open-ended: apcore-python used `hasattr(step, key)`, which accepted any attribute of the concrete class and made a working config non-portable to the other two SDKs.
driver_contract.steps_entries_are_closed_too: `$defs/PipelineStep` is `additionalProperties: false`. A driver needs a step TYPE registered under the fixture's `type` value to reach the insertion path at all — register a no-op step type named by the case rather than rewriting the case to use a built-in, since the point is the unknown key on an otherwise valid insertion.
